blogs.title: Hiccups and Hyponatremia: A Triad to Watch for CNS Inflammation
blogs.description: This post uses the case of a man with severe hyponatremia and persistent hiccups to highlight a key physical exam clue. It explores why hiccups can be a marker for metabolic disturbance (SIADH) secondary to CNS pathology, and reviews the safety protocols for managing severe hyponatremia in the ICU setting to prevent rhabdomyolysis and neurologic injury.

blogs.title: When the MRI is Normal: The Diagnostic Trap in Neuro-Behçet's Disease
blogs.description: Focusing on the case where typical parenchymal lesions were absent on MRI, this blog teaches the limitations of neuroimaging in meningoencephalitic syndromes. It outlines the rationale for prioritizing CSF analysis over radiological findings in suspicious cases of neuro-inflammatory conditions, and clarifies when to consider parenchymal-sparing variants of Behçet's.

blogs.title: Beyond Steroids: The Role of Colchicine Monotherapy in Acute Neuro-Inflammation
blogs.description: This article analyzes the surprising management success with colchicine alone instead of systemic steroids. It discusses the pharmacological differences between colchicine and immunosuppressants, the risks of steroid-induced relapse in Behçet's, and presents a risk-benefit framework for considering colchicine as a first-line agent in specific low-risk vascular presentations.

blogs.title: The 5-Point Rule: Diagnosing Behçet's Syndrome Without the HLA-B51 Marker
blogs.description: A deep dive into the International Criteria for Behçet's Disease, using the case patient's score as a walking example. This post examines the challenges of diagnosing BD concurrently with neurological symptoms, reviews the sensitivity/specificity of HLA-B51 testing (and why it's often not required), and provides a checklist for applying the International Conflict Guidelines in the emergency department.

blogs.title: Fever and Headache: The Infectious vs. Vasculitic Differential
blogs.description: This clinical pearl post focuses on the initial diagnostic triage for afebrile meningoencephalitis. Using the case's initial inappropriate antimicrobial treatment as a cautionary tale, it details the specific exclusionary workup needed to differentiate between HSV/VZV encephalitis, bacterial meningitis, and systemic autoimmune vasculitis before settling on a diagnosis of exclusion like Behçet's.
